result.title: Learning to Look: A Foundation for Visual Understanding
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) suffer from visual hallucination, such as saying an object that is not present in an image. We ask a more fundamental question: whether a VLM is even aware of where it is looking before understanding the semantic meaning in the image. We formulate this question as a LOOK task: identifying which parts of its visual input were available to the model. We construct the task in a self-supervised way without manually labeling the available region to the model. Our experiments show that existing VLMs fail to localize the visible region. We further show that fine-tuning VLMs on the proposed LOOK task improves a model's awareness of visual input.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出自监督的 LOOK 任务，要求 VLM 识别其视觉输入中哪些区域实际可见，并发现现有模型难以定位可见区域，而针对该任务微调可提升模型对视觉输入的感知。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接诊断 VLM 对「自己看到了什么」的内部可用性，与视觉证据筛选、位置/可见性状态表示及视觉幻觉相关，可供核查 LOOK 能力是否影响 latent 推理中的证据使用与停止决策。
